original_test_intent: Verify that a BMC Factory Default operation resets only the intended non-preserved settings while each explicitly selected Preserve item survives unchanged, and that the BMC returns to manageable healthy service.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT/firmware and authoritative factory-default/Preserve semantics; export all current settings and record the exact selected preserve matrix plus representative selected and unselected values; validate the supported UI/API action read-only; obtain approval and recovery access; invoke Factory Default once through the approved path; record outage/readiness; compare every preserved value unchanged and every governed non-preserved value to its documented default; verify accounts, network, security, logs and host/BMC health, then restore only the approved final configuration.
manual_activity: An authorized operator selects and visually confirms Preserve items, approves the destructive factory reset, watches recovery through an independent console and restores access if network or accounts reset.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT/firmware identity and vendor-supported Factory Default UI/API contract
Complete Preserve item list, exact selected matrix and representative selected/unselected before values
Documented defaults and rules for accounts, network, certificates, services, logs and other settings
Configuration export/backup, maintenance approval, credential-safe access, readiness timeout and physical/console recovery
safety_requirements: Verify the exact BMC and export recoverable configuration before any reset
Discover and approve the vendor action and payload; do not assume `Manager.Reset` accepts `FactoryReset`
Use trusted TLS and secret-safe authentication; do not print credentials
Preserve existing SEL/host evidence and correlate reset events by timestamp
Issue at most one approved reset; stop on lost access, partial defaults, unexpected preserved-item change, reset loop or host/BMC fault and invoke recovery without retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, vendor action, backup, preserve/default matrix, approval and recovery readiness
Collect read-only before state and post-recovery configuration comparisons
Invoke the exact approved one-shot action only after separate execution confirmation
Do not choose preserve items, infer defaults, disable TLS verification, expose secrets, clear logs, retry reset or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the Preserve matrix, default matrix and vendor reset action/scope
Approve outage/readiness limits, final desired state and recovery workflow
Review before/after evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: After vendor discovery, backup and approval, perform the documented Factory Default operation exactly once through WebUI or the vendor API, then query and compare the complete approved setting matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: WebUI Preserve selection, Start action, approximately three-minute reset expectation and preserve criterion remain; exact API, timeout and setting/default matrix require approval.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a paired before/after selected-versus-unselected configuration matrix around one approved vendor factory-default action, with independent recovery and access restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds authoritative action discovery, backup, default oracle, management outage/readiness and configuration-wide evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Firmware version, HTTP status or simple BMC reachability cannot prove Factory Default or Preserve semantics.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Network, users, certificates and trust anchors may reset and strand remote management; some preserved settings may activate only after a further reboot that must be explicitly documented.

review_improvement: Replaces firmware-only confirmation with the actual preservation/default oracle and prevents an unverified generic reset, credential exposure, evidence deletion and blind retry.
independent_technical_reasoning: Factory default is a configuration transformation, so success requires two complementary assertions: selected Preserve values remain identical and covered unselected values equal documented defaults. A management firmware read proves neither. Reset action vocabularies and payloads are implementation-specific, making vendor discovery mandatory before a destructive POST. Because accounts and network settings may be among the reset domains, recovery must not depend solely on the same management path being tested. A second reset cannot safely be used as an automatic retry.
